Optimal.Notes: A locked 40 fps at 40 Hz gives a perfectly smooth feel for a MOBA; medium textures keep gods and the battlefield looking respectable while FSR recovers sharpness from the reduced render resolution. This is the recommended starting point for most players.

profiles.Summary: SMITE is a DirectX 11 third-person MOBA that is technically unsupported on Steam Deck but runs at silver/gold tier under Proton, with most players getting into matches after some configuration. The Steam Deck's RDNA 2 GPU sits comfortably above the minimum spec, so 40–60 fps at medium-low settings is realistic, though online-only gameplay and occasional Proton quirks can affect the experience.
profiles.BasisNote: No Steam Deck-specific reports were available; profiles are estimated from SMITE's PC minimum/recommended requirements compared against the Deck's RDNA 2 GPU (roughly GTX 1050 Ti class). On first launch, verify EasyAntiCheat works under your chosen Proton version, then check frame rate during a busy teamfight and adjust settings accordingly.

MaxBattery.Notes: Rendering at sub-native resolution with FSR upscaling keeps the GPU load very low; shadows and AO are the biggest power draws in SMITE and disabling them saves significant wattage. GE-Proton is recommended based on general community preference for Hi-Rez titles under Linux.

KnownIssues: Game is marked Unsupported on Steam Deck — the Hi-Rez launcher or login screen may cause issues requiring workarounds or specific Proton versions.
Anti-cheat (EasyAntiCheat) has historically caused launch failures; verify it is functional under the chosen Proton version before investing time.
In-game text and UI elements can appear small at 1280x800 without adjusting the HUD scale setting.
Online-only title: network latency and server connectivity must be confirmed; no offline mode available.

MaxPerformance.Notes: Native resolution at high settings is achievable in quieter moments but teamfight particle effects can push the GPU hard and cause dips into the mid-40s; if frame rate is unstable, drop Shadow Quality to Low and Effects Quality to Medium first. Battery life will be short at full TDP.

Optimal.Notes: GE-Proton gives the best chance of bypassing launcher issues. Medium textures at a sub-native render resolution with FSR delivers a clean image while maintaining a stable 40 fps during teamfights.

profiles.Summary: SMITE is a third-person MOBA with moderate PC requirements that should run acceptably on the Steam Deck, though its "Unsupported" Verified status and silver ProtonDB tier suggest some friction getting it running — likely due to its Epic Online Services/Hi-Rez launcher or anti-cheat layer. Once in-game, the RDNA 2 GPU comfortably meets the minimum spec, so 40–60 fps is achievable at low-medium settings.
profiles.BasisNote: No Deck-specific reports were available; profiles are estimated from PC minimum/recommended specs versus Deck GPU capability and the known launcher/anti-cheat hurdles. On first run, verify the Hi-Rez/Epic launcher completes successfully with GE-Proton, then check frame rate in a busy teamfight and drop to Max Battery settings if it dips below 35 fps.

MaxBattery.Notes: GE-Proton is recommended to help bypass Hi-Rez launcher issues. Dropping to 960x600 with FSR upscaling keeps the GPU load low and extends battery life significantly during long sessions.

Anti-cheat (EAC) integration may block online play on Linux/Proton, potentially limiting to offline modes
In-game framerate cap and vsync settings may conflict with Steam Deck Quick Access frame limits
Steam Deck 'Unsupported' status suggests the launcher or online services have not been verified to work reliably

MaxPerformance.Notes: Running at native 1280x800 with no TDP cap lets the APU boost freely; expect frame dips during large teamfights with heavy particle effects. Disable Motion Blur to keep the image clean and reduce GPU load.
